name: Red Squirrel Recovery Network Community Grants Scheme

administered_by.name: Red Squirrel Recovery Network (Northumberland Wildlife Trust)

summary: Micro and small grants for community groups and not-for-profits doing red squirrel conservation, including habitat improvement, in northern England and southern Scotland. Grey squirrel control costs are excluded.

geography.label: Northumberland, Cumbria, Scottish Borders, Dumfries & Galloway, South Ayrshire and parts of Lancashire/Merseyside

amount.note: Micro grants under £500, small grants £500 to £5,000.

reporting: Micro grants: a brief report and photos on outcomes and spending within 4 weeks of completion. Small grants: a detailed report with financial summary and photos after completion.

status.quote: Micro Grants: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed monthly.

administered_by.quote: Funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund (TNLHF), the Red Squirrel Recovery Network (RSRN) is an ambitious five-year cross-border programme (2025-2030) working to prevent the extinction of the UK's native red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris). The RSRN project is a partner collaboration; involving Northumberland Wildlife Trust (NWT), Cumbria Wildlife Trust (CWT)

applicant_types.quote: The Community Grants Scheme provides micro grants (under £500) and small grants (£500 to £5,000) to community groups and not-for-profit organisations.

geography.quote: the Red Squirrel Recovery Network area that covers Northumberland, Cumbria, Scottish Borders, Dumfries & Galloway, South Ayrshire and areas of Lancashire/Merseyside

access.quote: Submit the completed application form and budget breakdown online.

window.quote: Small Grants: Applications are reviewed quarterly.

amount.quote: it is unlikely the RSRN Community Grants Scheme will support grants larger than £5,000.

reporting.quote: A brief report and photographs detailing project outcomes and expenditure must be submitted within 4 weeks of project completion.
